Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Fire-then-extinguish: transient stimulus with AP-1 chromatin tracking
ideas.description: Give cells a brief stimulus (e.g., TPA, injury, or cytokine; the 'fire'), then measure after the stimulus is gone whether AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding, accessibility (ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN) and target gene primed responses persist for days to weeks. Compare naive vs. pre-exposed cells on re-stimulation to quantify faster or stronger transcription, which is the hallmark of memory.

ideas.title: Acute degradation of AP-1 at defined windows
ideas.description: Use dTAG/AID degron alleles or dominant-negative (A-FOS) to remove AP-1 either during the initial stimulus, during the resting interval, or during restimulation. If memory needs AP-1 only to establish it, or also to maintain it, this separates the two roles and shows whether AP-1 is necessary and not just correlated.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome lineage-tracked heritability
ideas.description: Pair scATAC/scRNA multiome with lineage barcodes or sister-cell pair analysis to test whether AP-1-opened chromatin states and gene expression are inherited across divisions in a clonal pattern. Compare the persistence of these states with that of cells with matched exposure but no AP-1 activation to see whether the 'symmetry' of memory between sister cells exceeds chance.

ideas.title: Live-cell reporters of AP-1 dynamics and feedback
ideas.description: Image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN and a target-gene reporter in single cells over repeated pulses, measuring whether history changes the amplitude, timing, or the bistable on/off state. Fit mathematical models (positive feedback, hysteresis) to test whether memory arises from self-sustaining AP-1 circuit dynamics versus slow chromatin changes.

ideas.title: Sufficiency test by synthetic AP-1 activation and chromatin editing
ideas.description: Induce AP-1 artificially (optogenetic or chemogenetic JUN/FOS, or dCas9-tethered AP-1 at selected enhancers) in naive cells, then withdraw it and ask whether the enhancer stays open, retains H3K27ac, and responds more strongly later. Control with DNA-binding or transactivation mutants and test the contribution of cofactors such as the BAF complex, which tests sufficiency for memory-like states.
